description:
FILED s538a (Opus, 2026-11-13) from a probe beside s537a's #4762 (a leading `::` names main).  PRE-EXISTING: main 53dd73da
(MAIN-READY-88), the old base 23f0f917 and the s538a tree all answer the same.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3; the s538a worktree's scratch/s538a/pr2/colonfh.pl):

    my $f = "/tmp/x$$"; open my $w, ">", $f or die; print $w "x\ny\n"; close $w;
    open(::H, "<", $f) or die; my $a = <::H>; print "1 '", ($a // "undef") =~ s/\n//r, "'\n";
    my @r = <::H>; print "2 n=", scalar(@r), "\n"; close ::H;
    open(H2, "<", $f) or die; my $b = readline(::H2); print "3 '", ($b // "undef") =~ s/\n//r, "'\n";

  perl:  1 'x'      2 n=1     3 'x'
  PCL:   1 '::H'    2 n=1     3 'undef'

Row 1: `<::H>` is not recognised as a bareword handle (the angle operand test wants a plain identifier or a
`Pkg::NAME`, so `::H` falls to the GLOB branch and the pattern "::H" comes back as itself, #450's literal-word
rule).  Row 3: `readline(::H2)` resolves the handle to the package "" or reads a fresh symbol.  Row 2 agreeing is an
accident (the glob's one element).  Same family as #452 (`<main::FH2>`, fixed s438g by widening `_bareword_fh_p`)
and #4762's ONE splitter `%p-split-symbolic-name`: a leading `::` is main.  Fix at the angle-operand predicate
(the same one that serves `print ::H` -- that one works) and the readline argument's handle resolution; probe
`eof(::H)`, `close ::H` (works), `<::H>` in list context, `while (<::H>)`.  LOW (a rare spelling; found in a
package section `package Bar; open(::H, ...); <::H>`).
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing): a handle named with a leading `::` in a READ slot -- `<::H>` is the glob pattern "::H" and `readline(::H)` reads nothing (undef); perl reads main::H in both (`open(::H, ...)` and `print ::H` work)
